distinguishing_features: Active, feedback-controlled fluid gap modulation via a secondary reservoir and valve
Directly targets hydrodynamic pressure fluctuations to break phase-locking in a self-excited wave phenomenon
Uses real-time modulation without altering the solid geometry of the roll
Implements a damping mechanism via out-of-phase pressure injection into the press gap
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Mitigating periodic gloss bands (barring) in paper calenders without requiring roll removal or permanent geometric changes, while adapting to varying operating conditions.
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism relies on injecting fluid into a high-pressure, micron-scale elastohydrodynamic lubrication gap at high frequencies, which is physically implausible due to the extreme precision, response times, and sealing challenges involved.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Even if viable, applying active damping to a rotating mechanical system using fluid injection is a known engineering approach for vibration control, making it an obvious extension of prior art.
